### RESPONSE
### Aircraft Incidents
### Safety
### PROP PLANES
- Clear distance of **5m** radius from front of plane
- Approach spinning propellers from **rear** only
- Do not interfere with **inactive** propellers
- Do not **walk** under wings

### JET PLANES
- Ear **protection** is worn
- Isolate **fuel** supply and shut down **engine**
- **Avoid** blast area (rear of engines) at all times
- Maintain **8m** clearance from jet **intake** area

### HELO'S
- Approach and leave helicopter in **crouched** position in **front** view of pilot
- Approach from **downhill** side only on uneven ground
- Carry all equipment below **waist** level

### Category (designates carrying capacity of aircraft)
- Level 1 – **up to 18 seats**
- Level 2 – **up to 215 seats** ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM
- Level 3 – **up to 450 seats**

### Generic Actions
### AIRCRAFT GENERIC ACTIONS **AIRMEN** ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM (short answer)
- **A**PPROACH from either nose or tail directing streams along fuselage, Avoid wheels area – dry powder only
- **I**NSULATE/isolate crew/passengers from fire using foam/water sprays
- Clear **R**ESCUE path to door using water/foam sprays
- **M**AINTAIN path to enable escape route **OR** access path for FFs
- **E**VACUATE passengers from plane immediately. **ATTEND** to fire/fuel spill
- **N**EXT appliance on scene act as backup/supply water/foam

### Airports
### Definitions
- **FULL EMERG** – aircraft **known** or **suspected** to be in danger of accident ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM
- **CRASH ON AIRPORT** – self-evident. Plane **seen** or is **about** to crash ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM

### Melbourne Airport - Actions
**Seek guidance from ARFF, turn off lights in airport**

**R R C O F E L**
- **R**espond to designated emergency access gate
- **R**equest all additional info from CommCen (Firecom)
- **C**omms with Aviation Rescue (ARFF) via Ch 52
- **O**btain directions from control tower or ASA Safety Officer
- **F**wdCmdPost indicated by **FLASHING BLUE LIGHT**

*(Melbourne Airport – Actions RRCOFEL, continued)*
- **E**xercise extreme caution crossing runways/taxiways
- **L**iaise with airport/FF personnel on scene

### Bushfire
### BUSH FIRE SAFETY ACRONYM **L A C E S**
- **L**ookouts – **fixed/aerial/mobile** lookout deployed 2 maintain **appreciation** of **risk** and **advise** on need to use **escape routes** and **safety zones**
- **A**wareness - of changes in fire **behavior** due to variations in – **fuel/weather/topography** & other fire ground **hazards**
- **C**ommunications – all to follow agreed Comms Plan to discuss safety issues
- **E**scape Routes – **TWO** agreed and made **aware** by all AND **reviewed**
- **S**afety Zones – **identified** and **known** to all. Consider escape **time** and safety zone **size** that will change as **fire behaviour** changes

### Car Parks Incorporating Multi-Tiered Vehicle Stacking/Storage Devices (Car Stackers)
### Consideration (A6C)
- **ACCESS** to recessed parking pits not guaranteed
- **CONSIDER** – **PPV** or **INSTALLED** MECHANICAL **VENTILATION** for visibility
- Consider **DEFENSIVE** attack
- Consider **FOAM** fire attack
- Concerns regard for **FIREWATER**
- Consider building **POWER ISOLATION**

*(Car Stackers – Consideration (A6C), continued)*
- Consider **HART**

### ACTIONS ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM (short answer)
- **Isolate** electricity to car stacker – lock out/tag power supply
- Use **electrical current detector** to test for live equipment before proceeding with any **firefighting operations**
- Ascertain if **sprinklers activated** or **installed**
- Regularly conduct DRA

### CityLink
### Fire/HAZMAT
- **Confirm** location of fire from TCR and close tunnel to traffic
- Consider use of **telephone** system in tunnels
- **Evac tunnel** as required via emergency access point or use safe havens in tunnel
- **Respond VicPol** assist Evac

### Within tunnels
- IC shall try to contain pollutants to site (major inc pollutants can be permitted down drains)
- Minor Inc managed at road surface level

### Open Roads
- Pollutants managed at road level
- IC consider bunding drains, applying absorbent etc

### Minor hazardous incidents/petrol washaways
- **CONFIRM LOCATION** of incident and request **ADJACENT LANE** closure to incident (from TCR). **Or close tunnel.**
- **CONTROL POLLUTANTS** in tunnels & open road level as above
- **DO NOT USE SAND**
- Check **HYDROCARBON** alarms installed in **UNDERGROUND PIT and above filtration tanks** and if operated, flush drainage system until alarm reset

### Electric and hybrid vehicles
### Actions
- Approach from side
- Chock wheels, apply park brake
- Place transmission into Park
- Stabilise if not on four wheels
- ***Note:*** *After disabling the HV battery pack, power is maintained for 90 seconds in the airbags and up to 10 minutes in the high voltage electrical system.* ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM
### Generic Information for all motor vehicle incidents/fires
### Considerations
- Availability of water supply (respond WT or PT if req)
- Fuel Source (petrol, gas, elec...)
- Undeployed airbags
- Once 12v battery is disconnected, handbrake may not engage/disengage

### LPG powered vehicles
### Safety
- Do **not extinguish** burning if **gas** still **venting**; **LEAVE TO BURN**
- Be aware of **increase** in **fire intensity/ pitch** of escaping gas; **SITUATION DETERIORATING**
- **EVACUATE** if suspected of rupturing
- Do not direct water at **VENTING PRESSURE GAUGE** - icing
### Actions
**During Fire**
- Utilize hose lines from **SHELTERED POSITION** where possible
- Cool cylinder with flooding quantities of water onto upper surfaces until **well after** fire is out
- Use dry chem, CO2 or water spray to **EXT FIRE** (only if **absolutely necessary** AND **safe to do so**)

### Trams
### Considerations
- Trams operate **600V** DC tractive control from overhead trolley wire
- **POWER CONTROL CENTRAL** able to ISOLATE POWER TO SECTIONS of the network remotely.
- **ISOLATION** not guaranteed until maintenance crews arrive
- Respond **Heavy Rescue Pod**
- Tram roof = **HART**

### Dangerous Goods
### BOILERS
**Considerations:** Consider **site evacuation**

### Actions
Turn off using:
- Emergency stop buttons
- Burner switch
- Main isolation switch

If unable to shut down or turn off boiler:
- Attempt to maintain water level in boiler
- Reduce steam pressure to lowest pressure

### Pressure Vessels
### Safety
- Identify contents prior to application of water onto exposed surface as water can cause heat reaction
- Possible BLEVE
### Considerations
- Consider site evacuation
- Consider utilising TIC
### Actions
- Liaise with onsite specialist
- Secure the scene
- Protect exposures and contain
- Attempt to control with fuel isolation or dry agents
- Liaise with onsite specialist

Ascertain:
- Vessel contents
- Can the vessel be isolated/turned off?
- Can the vessel be depressurised?
### Specialist contacts / Notifications
Plant Managers, operators and onsite specialist

NOTIFY – WorkSafe Victoria

### Flammable Metals
### Safety
- Exercise extreme caution due to: Possible spontaneous heating or combustion
- High risk of explosion for metal dust or powder
- Storage potentially being in flammable liquid – kerosene,
### Actions
**DO NOT USE WATER** as extinguishing agent – creates violent reaction

### Gas Flare Off - LPG
Able to flare-off LPG cylinders (vehicle and other) **up to 200kg**.

LPG flare-off operation is to be implemented at incidents involving leaking LPG cylinders, where the **leak cannot be isolated**.
### Considerations
- Location of incident for evacuation and possible **ignition sources**
- Cylinder size – **max 200kg**
- Flare-off operations can only take place with a minimum of **two gas flare-off operators** on scene
- Atmospheric monitoring equipment to determine flammability
- VicPol and Ambulance Victoria response

### Gas Mains / Natural Gas
ACTIONS
### With Fire ...GAAS
- **G**as Company for **IMMEDIATE** response
- **A**pproach from safe direction
- **A**scertain whether supply can be **shut off**
- Protect **exposures**
### Without Fire ...GEtFUQD
- **G**as Company for **IMMEDIATE** response
- **E**liminate ignition sources **30mts** minimum
- (t)
- **F**ully charged **line**. Dissipate gas in exceptional circumstances
- **U**pwind approach with **appropriate** PPC
- **Q**REA for gas monitoring
- **D**rychem on standby
### Inside/Confined Space
- **Evacuate**
- Use personal **gas monitor** to monitor gas **concentration** (%LEL)
- **Ventilate** until **personal** gas monitor **alarm** ceases
- Shut off **gas** when **safe** to do so

### Major Hazardous Facilities / Refineries
### Actions — FFLLEES BMW(M)
- **FIRST APPLIANCE** on scene report to INCIDENT SUPPORT CENTRE
- **FOLLOWING APPLIANCES** report to STAGING AREA
- **LOCATE** and ACCESS emergency information container (front gate/nr entrance)
- **LIASE** with on-site EMERGENCY SUPERVISOR
- **ESTABLISH LOCATION** and access to fire/spill
- **EVACUATE** area
- **SEND** regular sitreps
- **BOOST** hydrants/sprinklers
- **MAINTAIN** appliance FLASHING lights in MHF
- **WEAR** ear/eye protection
- **MONITOR** wind direction/weather reports

### Electrical
### Aerial Appliances - Safety
- Use a **spotter** near powerline ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM
- Clearance for EWP **3m** no go zone **poles**
- **8m** no go zone **Towers**
### Electrical Substations / Substation yards ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM (short answer)
- **Firefighters** shall not **enter** unless **accompanied** by an electrical supply **company representative** or other **trained/authorised** persons.

### Pole Fires – Actions ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM (short answer)
- **Power Co.** requested immediately
- Do not attempt **extinguish** until power company confirm **isolation** or confirm area safe before extinguishing
- Protect **exposures**
- Attack fire **ONLY** to protect life by;
  - **Fog** or broken stream (no jet)
  - **Lob** onto fire
  - Avoid **wires**
  - Don't **stand** in water/wet surfaces
### Uninterrupted Power Supplies (UPS)
Treat as live, isolate power between electrical equipment and UPS, ESC to respond to ensure power is isolated
- UPS may be present when dealing with **computers**, **telephone exchanges**, **process controllers**.
- Treat all such **equipment** as **live**.
- **Isolate** power between **electrical equipment** and **UPS**.
- Request power supply company to **respond** to ensure power **isolation**

### LPG
### Properties
- DG IERG GUIDE 04
- UN **1075** ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM
- HAZCHEM: **2YE**
- Exp ratio **270:1**
- LEL **1.5%** UEL **10%**

### LPG (Properties, continued)
- **Heavier** than air, will collect in low areas
- LPG cylinder **silver**, bullets **White**

### Fire Investigation
### Response Criteria of Fire Investigators
- All **fire** related **deaths**
- All **fire** related **serious** injuries
- Fires where the **origin** and cause cannot be easily **determined**
- Notification at **3rd alarm** and **automatic** FIA response at **4th alarm** or greater at structure fires (MFB)
- Any firefighter **injury** (MFB)
- Fires involving fire brigade **property**
- MFB Fire Investigation will not attend **suspicious** fires unless **requested** by **VicPol**
### Considerations
- Obstacles preventing entry into building access/firefighting
- Extent of fire on arrival
- locations / intensity / colour of flames/smoke
- Indications of forcible entry
- Conditions of doors / windows

### Hospitals
### Actions
| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Code RED | Fire, smoke |
| Code PURPLE | Bomb threat, extortion, suspicious package |
| Code ORANGE | Evacuation |
| Code YELLOW | Explosion, person trapped, chemical emergency |
| Code GREY | Patient violent, patient restraint |
| Code BLACK | Non patient violence, armed/unarmed intrusion, armed patient violence |
| Code BLUE | Medical emergency |
| Code BROWN | State disaster, major incident, internal accident |

**Code Black** ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM

### Secured Facility Response ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM
### Actions
- Meet with facility Liaison Officer (LO) and Field Comm (FC) at entrance to site
- OIC to ascertain nature and status of event, status of secured facility and assess situation
- Enter on only req by Facility Management, if site security is confirmed, and only under guidance of escort/liaison officer (one per appl)
- If req to enter and is deemed safe to do so, and if need arises, IC notify Ops Comm
- FSV personnel to receive briefing by facility staff incl arrangements for emerg evac plan
- Min number of appl and crew to be committed, IC to determine
- Routine security checks undertaken in consideration of situation
- FSV to withdraw if safety/security of personnel/appl becomes threatened
- Security checks on departure. LO to confirm absence of prisoners on appl
- IC to confirm ID of FF leaving secured Facility

*FRV Incident Management System – AIIMS Advice Card (P935, Version 5, February 2024)*

#### Incident Management Team (IMT)
Comprises the Incident Controller (IC) and a team of people (determined by the complexity, scale and needs of the situation) to safely resolve an incident and support recovery.

#### Incident Emergency Management Team (IEMT)
An inter-agency team which supports the IC in formulating and implementing response and recovery strategies. Includes VicPol, AV, local government, power/gas, etc.

#### Incident Controller (IC)
- Establish incident control point.
- Assess the situation, identify risks and determine priorities.
- Develop, authorise, implement and monitor Incident Action Plan (IAP).
- Authorise community warnings and advice.
- Communicate impact, risk and progress to all affected parties and FRV Senior Command.
- Establish and maintain an IMT and IEMT.
- Appoint Deputy ICs as required.
- Facilitate transfer of control where required to an ICC.
- Monitor and review safety and welfare of all involved and appoint Safety Officers/Safety Cell.
- Consider implementing Medical IMT through 24/7 FRV Health Incident Triage Service (1800 378 432).
- Establish a Personnel Accountability Report (PAR) process.
- Facilitate media management.
- Conclude and review activities.

#### Deputy Incident Controller
- Reports to and supports IC.
- Undertakes the role of IC in their absence.
- Oversee function units as required, e.g. Operations.
- Manage one or more particular functions, e.g. Evacuation, Business Continuity, Warnings and Advice, Media, etc.

#### Agency Commander
- Appointed at incidents where FRV resources are deployed, but FRV is **not** the Control Agency.
- Can be used as Deputy IC for smaller scale incidents or outside line of control.
- Establish contact with IC/OO from other agency.
- Provide communication link and advice to other agencies.
- Provide communication link from fireground to FRV SOC.
- Represent FRV at any IEMT.

#### Incident Safety Officer
Not a functional role, but reports directly to the IC and is part of the IMT.
- Manage Safety Cell at 3rd alarm and higher and at complex or protracted incidents. Appoint:
  - Field Safety Commander
  - Health and Safety Representative
  - DEBRiS Officer
  - Base of Operations Officer
  - Appliance and Recommissioning Officer
  - Notify FRV Health if required (peer support, ground/medical support).
- Develop and maintain Incident Safety Plan.
- Provide advice on safety and overall health and safety of personnel at incident.
- Liaise with IC, Field Safety Officer(s) and Field Safety Commander.
- Ensure that IC and IMT focus on safety.
- Provide and review input to IAP.

#### Field Safety Commander
- Provides safety awareness to Incident Safety Officer.
- Monitors safe systems of work at the incident and the base of operations.
- Ensure all components of the Safety Plan are operating effectively.
- Advises Incident Safety Officer of any resourcing requirements.
- Engages assistance from HSR.

#### Field Safety Officer
- Responsible through chain of command to Sector Commander, OO and IC.
- Preferably rank of SO or above.
- Check general structural safety (walls, roofing, etc.).
- Ensure use of appropriate procedures (e.g. PPC, PPE, hazmat, BA, asbestos, high rise).
- Communicate risks/problems immediately to OO/IC/Incident Safety Officer/Sector Commander.
- Report near misses, accidents, injuries and ensure they are followed up.
- IC may allocate more than one Safety Officer depending on incident complexity.

#### Planning Officer (PO)
- Identify current objectives, strategies and resources required.
- Develop IAP and populate eIAP.
- Develop options analysis and alternative objectives and strategies.
- Assess current and future risks (e.g. weather, hazmat, fire water runoff).
- Monitor resources requested, en-route, allocated to, and released from the incident.
- Provide information to Public Information Officer and IMT (via sitreps).
- Develop communications plan.
- Prepare report for IC at incident conclusion.

#### Public Information Officer (PIO)
- Prepare community Warnings and Advice (W&A) at request of IC; obtain authorisation from IC before issuing.
- Liaise with OO on risks and PO to ensure W&A are tailored, timely, relevant and accessible.
- Types of W&A: Community Information; Advice; Watch and Act; Emergency Warning (Prepare to Evacuate, Evacuate Now, Safe to Return).
- Format of community W&A: verbal messages (door knock); EMCOP (advice/watch/act/evacuation); Emergency Alert (telephone warning system, mobile and landline); Standard Emergency Warning Signal (SEWS); radio and TV.
- Format of community information: media conference/interview/release; newsletters.
- Ensure "advice – all clear" is given when incident or community risk has subsided.
- Manage W&A, Community Liaison and Media Units.

#### Logistics Officer (LO)
- Obtain resources (human and physical), facilities, services and materials to support IMT.
- Monitor current and expected resources.
- Assist PO to produce communications plan.
- Establish staging area and rehabilitation requirements if not already established under DEBRiS.
- Develop Logistics section of IAP.

#### Operations Officer (OO)
- Brief the IC on current strategies when handing over control.
- Establish operational structure (sectors, staging, BA, decontamination and rehabilitation as required).
- Allocate resources to enable safe work practices to be implemented.
- Manage and monitor progress of operations and provide regular progress reports (sitreps) to IC.
- Implement IAP and request additional resources if required.
- Implement process for briefing incoming personnel (SMEACS).
- Identify current and emerging risks.
- Manage and communicate risks to IC and IMT.
- Facilitate PAR when required.

**Structure under Operations – Sector Commander**
- Implement portion of IAP relevant to their sector.
- Allocate and manage resources within sector.
- Report to OO on progress of operations, emerging risks and status of resources including personnel.
- Sector names can be: **Geographical** (1 = front, 2 = left side, 3 = rear, 4 = right side – clockwise); **Functional** (staging, evacuation, hazmat, etc.); **High rise** (evacuation sector, lobby sector, fire sector).
- Facilitate PAR for sector when required.

**Staging Officer**
- Establish staging area and communication with OO.
- Establish all appliances and personnel on scene using Fireground Accountability System.
- Deploy resources requested by OO.
- When directed, maintain a reserve of two primary appliances with personnel.
- At 3rd alarm and above fires and Hazmat incidents should be SSO or above.

**DEBRiS Officer**
- Establish and oversee DEBRiS system and workflow appropriate to the requirements of the incident.
- At 3rd alarm and above fires and Hazmat incidents, all sectors of DEBRiS must be implemented, and the DEBRiS Officer must be SSO or above.
- Appoint Base of Operations, Decontamination Officer, BA Service Officer, Rehabilitation Officer, Staging Officer, RIT Teams.
- Consider environmental conditions.
- Ensure all PPC and equipment bagged and tagged appropriately.

#### Intelligence, Finance and Investigation
Usually incorporated into the Planning, Logistics and Operations functions respectively. The IC may determine that the complexity, scale or nature of an incident requires separate functions be established.
- **Intelligence Officer:** determine intelligence required; collect and analyse information (current and forecasted); make sense of information (what does it mean?); record, distribute and display situation reports; provide PO with information to support development of IAP.
- **Finance Officer:** oversee financial management and record keeping during incident.
- **Investigation Officer:** determine cause/factors which contributed to the impact of incident; when an external investigative authority (e.g. police) is responsible, act as liaison on behalf of IC; determine effectiveness of response and examine unexpected events during response.

#### State Emergency Management Priorities
These underpin and guide all decisions during response to any emergency:
1. Protection and preservation of life is paramount: safety of emergency services personnel; safety of community members including vulnerable community members and visitors/tourists.
2. Issuing of community information and warnings detailing incident information that is timely, relevant and tailored to assist community members make informed decisions about their safety.
3. Protection of critical infrastructure and community assets that supports community resilience.
4. Protection of residential property as a place of primary residence.
5. Protection of assets supporting individual livelihoods and economic production that supports individual and community financial sustainability.
6. Protection of environment and conservation values including cultural, biodiversity and social values.

#### Briefing format – SMEACSQ
- **Situation:** overview of incident, type/status; current/unexpected weather, behaviour; life and property at risk; deployed resources overview; agencies involved.
- **Mission:** incident objectives (SMART); what are we trying to protect/prepared to lose; time frames for set goals.
- **Execution:** sectorisation; strategies and tactics; constraints; task and resource allocation; safe access/egress to incident/sectors; timeframes for select tasks; community warnings issued.
- **Administration and logistics:** logistics of operation; key support locations/roles (ops points, ICC, staging area, water points, DEBRiS); catering/accommodation.
- **Command and Communication:** allocation of key IMT roles; communications plan; communications problems.
- **Safety:** weather forecast changes/impacts; known/anticipated hazards; safety equipment/PPE; welfare (hydration/first aid/rehabilitation); Red Flag Warnings issued; welfare issues; incident OH&S incidents; LACES (Lookout, Awareness, Communication, Escape Routes, Safety Zones).
- **Questions:** questions/input/issues.

#### Interviews/Briefing – Aide Memoir
- What we know
- What we don't know
- What we are doing
- What we want you to do

### Chapter 3 - Breathing Apparatus Operational and Safety Procedures
**Duties of Breathing Apparatus Control Officer (BACO)**

The duties of the BACO are as follows:
- Supervise BA service, entry points and all BA requirements.
- Set up the Emergency Signal Unit (ESU).
- As directed by the IC, have an adequate number of firefighters available and dressed in BA as reliefs, and to order them to the appropriate BA entry in time to enable operational personnel to carry out their responsibilities.
- Liaise with BA entry, BA service.
- Liaise with the IC and Operations Officer on BA strategies and tactics and send periodic reports to the IMT.
- Notify the IC of unaccounted firefighters for activation of relief crews.

**Duties of BA Entry Officer (BAEO)**

The duties of the person in charge of BA entry are as follows:
- Establish a BA control board at the BA entry point and obtain the tally tags of BA operators operating from that point.
- Relieve firefighters at the appropriate time according to the record.
- As directed by the IC, have sufficient firefighters standing by for relief purposes throughout the time the BA entry is operating.
- Have at least two (2) firefighters standing by dressed in BA for emergency purposes.

*(BAEO duties, continued)*
- Initiate a relief team in consultation with the IC when necessary, such as firefighters failing to report when due out.
- Conduct a Personnel Accountability Report (PAR) if requested.
- Send periodic reports to the BACO indicating the number of BA in use, personnel requirements.

### Chapter 7 - Ancillary Equipment
- Level A protective suit (fully encapsulating suit) ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM
- Level B protective suit (splash suit)
- Level D protective clothing (structural firefighter ensemble)

**Survival mask – located BA38**

### Operational Method Statements (OMS)
### OMS 001 - Incident Management
2.7.2. Ensure the IEMT meets formally during a fire/incident to be provided a **SMEACSQ** briefing. This is to be done at regular times in a safe location.

### Location Control Point Consideration
**2 Actions** for Establishing ICP
1. **Establish an Incident Control Point at every fire/incident.** This is the responsibility of the OIC of the first arriving appliance
2. **Name each ICP** and communicate the name to the Comm Centre.

1.2.1 Establish an incident control point, taking the following considerations; ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM
- Ease of access
- Prominence of location with a good overview of the incident
- Ability to stage and deploy all arriving appliances and support agency personnel
- Safety from any incident hazards
- Potential impediments to incident communications

Implement an Incident Management System

Manage all fire/incidents in accordance with the following **AIIMS** principles (MUFFS) ⭐ PREVIOUS EXAM
- Management by objectives
- Functions management
- Span of control
- Flexibility
- Unity of command

### OMS003 - Incident Sectors
- SECTOR 1 – FRONT
- SECTOR 2 – LEFT
- SECTOR 3 - REAR
- SECTOR 4 – RIGHT SIDE

HIGH RISE - SECTOR OF BUILDING FOLLOWED BY FLOOR NUMBER (level), eg 2-14

### OMS 005 - Size Up
**Utilise B-SAHF during Size Up at a structure fire:**
- **B**uilding – construction style/materials that impact fire behaviour
- **S**moke – volume, velocity, density, and colour
- **A**ir track – inlets and outlets, what is the building ventilation profile?
- **H**eat – blackening/crazing of windows, blistering of paintwork
- **F**lame – colour (yellow/red/blue), indicator of oxygen supply to fire

**Ensure the following principles are included in Size Up:**
- **Facts** – What do you know that is affecting the incident, mitigation and safety?
- **Probabilities** – What is likely to happen, including potential for fire spread and risk to life?
- **Own situation** – Do you have sufficient resources and capabilities? Should you respond more?
- **Decision** – What is your objective for the incident?
- **Plan** – How do you plan to resolve the incident, and what strategies and tactics will be applied?

### OMS 012 - Situation Reports
### Strategic Level Situation Report
2.1. Strategic Level Situation Reports are to contain information relevant to the incident strategies and objective(s).

### Tactical Level Situation Report
3.1. Tactical Level Situation Reports are to only contain information relevant to an assigned task and must be kept brief

**3.3. Use the CAN format for all Tactical Level Situation Reports:**
- **C**onditions – What are the current conditions of the incident/task?
- **A**ctions – What actions are being implemented?
- **N**eeds – What additional resources are required?

### OMS 013 - Communications - Personnel Accountability Report (PAR)
When to conduct a PAR? 2.1
- Receipt of a **MAYDAY** msg
- Use of the **emergency evacuation signal**
- A change from **offensive to defensive** strategies
- Crews are **failing respond**

Who can request a PAR? 2.3
- Incident Controller IC
- Operations Officer
- Safety Officer
- Sector commander
- BA entry officer (BAEO)

### OMS 014 - Communications - Red Flag Warnings
### Requirements for receiving a Red Flag Warning
4.1. Ensure personnel who receive a Red Flag Warning complete the following:
- Confirm the Red Flag Warning has been received immediately.
- Repeat the key points of the warning back to the sender to demonstrate understanding.
- Notify all responding and support agency personnel of the Red Flag Warning under your supervision/in reporting line.
- Obtain a confirmation from these personnel that they have received the warning.

Convey Red Flag Warnings by any appropriate means, including:
- Radio
- Telephone
- Written notice
- Verbal

### OMS 015 - Communications - Mayday Radio Messages
Issuing a Mayday Radio Message

1.1. **Transmit a Mayday immediately when in a life threatening situation, or when others are in a life threatening situation.**

1.2. Utilise the Radio Duress Alarm (where available) to initiate the Mayday, and immediately transmit the following:
- "Mayday, Mayday, Mayday"
- Name of person transmitting or unit/call sign
- Location
- Situation report/assignment/task
- Resources/assistance

### OMS 016 - Communications - Red Red Red Priority Signal
Issuing a Red, Red, Red Priority Signal

1.1. Transmit a **"Red, Red, Red"** signal to send an urgent message where extreme radio congestion exists, in order to gain priority access to Communications Centre and the fireground channel(s).

### OMS 017 - Emergency Evacuation Signal
1.1 When EES used
- Imminent structural collapse
- Bushfire burn over
- Landslip
- Uncontrolled release of gas

1.2 Who can use
- Incident Controller - IC
- Operations Officer - OO
- Sector Commander
- Strike Team/Task Force Leader
- Appliance OIC

2.3 How to use it
- 3 short blast, each for 1 second duration
- Wait 10 seconds and repeat
- Repeat this sequence until all personnel are accounted for

What are the 3 Emergency Evacuation signals - what do they sound like?
- Evacuation: **3 blasts at 1 second duration**
- Quiet or cease operations: **1 blast for 3 seconds**
- Resume operations: **1 blast for 3 seconds followed by 1 blast for 1 second**

### OMS 040 - Incident Communication Plans
**Determine the level of fireground communications required based on the scale of the incident and request additional radio channels where necessary:**
- **Fireground Communications** – to be used for firefighting and incident mitigation operations.
- **Command Communications** – to be used for command level incident management.

#### Purpose
This Operational Method Statement provides guidance regarding incident management requirements for all incidents. It is designed to guide Incident Controllers on how to safely and efficiently coordinate resources necessary for the timely resolution of an incident.

#### Scope
This Operational Method Statement applies to all FRV Incident Controllers.

#### Actions
Responsibilities of the OIC of the first arriving appliance

**1. Establish an Incident Control Point**
- **1.1** Establish an Incident Control Point at every fire/incident, considering the following:
  - Ease of access
  - Prominence of location with a good overview of the incident
  - Safety from any hazards
  - Potential impediments to incident communications.
- **1.2** Communicate the name of the Incident Control Point to the Communications Centre.
- **1.3** Where multiple appliances arrive on scene in a similar time frame, the highest ranking OIC will assume control of the incident, unless otherwise determined.
  - **1.3.1** Incident Controller must wear an Incident Controller tabard.

**Responsibilities of the Incident Controller**

**2. Establish Control**
- **2.1** Conduct an initial incident Size Up.
- **2.2** Take control of all resources at the fire/incident.
- **2.3** Task crews with initial response and mitigation strategies. Further develop strategies to form the basis of an Incident Action Plan (IAP).
- **2.4** Implement an Incident Management System, with consideration to the following.
  - **2.4.1** Manage fire/incident in accordance with the following AIIMS principles:
    - Safety first
    - Management by objectives
    - Functional management
    - Span of control
    - Flexibility
    - Unity of command
  - **2.4.2** Delegate functional roles where appropriate, ensuring roles assumed by appropriately qualified personnel, where necessary.
  - **2.4.3** Ensure all personnel performing functional roles wear a tabard.
  - **2.4.4** Create an Operations Point when incident increases in size or complexity.
    - **2.4.4.1** Appoint an Operations Officer where appropriate. Operations Officer will manage operational activities across the incident. Operations Officer reports to the Incident Controller.
  - **2.4.5** Create Incident Sectors and appoint Sector Commanders to delegate control of sectors/floors/specialisation to suitably qualified personnel were required. E.g. Sector 1 Commander, Hazmat Commander. Note: Sector Commanders will report to the Operations Officer.
- **2.5** Initiate Community Information/Warning messages as required.
- **2.6** Request separate fireground channels to aid communications within sectors, as required.
- **2.7** Establish an Incident Staging Area(s) and appoint an Incident Staging Officer to manage incoming resources.

**3. Establish Safety Systems**
- **3.1** Appoint an Incident Safety Officer to oversee all aspects of safety across the incident. Safety Officer reports to the Incident Controller.
- **3.2** Consider appointing Field Safety Officers within each sector. Sector Safety Officers report to their respective Sector Commander.
- **3.3** At 3rd alarm and above, or similar sized incidents (Non-GARS) the Safety Officer responsible for overseeing incident safety must initiate the Safety Cell.
- **3.4** Appoint a Field Safety Commander.

**4. Establish DEBRiS Management System (MS)**
- **4.1** Appoint a DEBRiS Officer to create a central point for managing personnel through the DEBRiS Management System. This may be the pump operator, LFF or SO at smaller scale incidents, but should be a minimum of SSO where available at larger scale incidents (3rd alarm and above or similar sized incidents (Non-GARS).
- **4.2** Ensure appropriate DEBRiS MS Functions are implemented relevant to the size and complexity of the incident and areas to perform each function are easily identifiable, e.g. BA Support indicating BA Service Area/DEBRiS cones
- **4.3** Consider establishing RIT, if appropriate.

**5. Additional responsibilities of the Incident Controller**
- **5.1** Provide regular Situation Reports.
- **5.2** Establish Incident Emergency Management Team (IEMT).
  - **5.2.1** Establish an IEMT for multi-agency fires/incidents to support response and recovery efforts.
  - **5.2.2** Ensure the IEMT meets formally during a fire/incident to be provided a SMEACSQ briefing. This is to be done at regular times in a safe location.
  - **5.2.3** Log/record details of all IEMT meetings.
- **5.3** Transfer control, as appropriate to the incident and where required.
- **5.4** Establish a Communications Plan that reflects the scale of the incident or all fires/incident.
- **5.5** Manage and track all resources.
  - **5.5.1** Track the location and tasking of all resources deployed to the fire/incident.
  - **5.5.2** Consider utilising maps or “mud maps” to assist in managing the fire/incident.
- **5.6** Initiate a Personnel Accountability Report (PAR) to account for resources, when appropriate.
- **5.7** Document and Maintain Logs and Records of pertinent incident information.
- **5.8** Consider requesting MERC to assist in organising emergency accommodation for displaced persons, and establishing scene security and safety, if required.

**6. Closing the Incident**
- **6.1** Conduct an incident debrief with the IEMT at the conclusion of the fire/incident.
- **6.2** Determine the cause of the fire.
  - **6.2.1** Request the attendance of the State Fire Investigation Unit (SFIU) where the cause of the fire cannot be determined.
  - **6.2.2** Request the attendance of Victoria Police where the cause of the fire is considered to be suspicious.
- **6.3** Ensure the scene is left safe and secure at the conclusion of operations.
- **6.4** Consider completing a Handover of Scene form.
- **6.5** Conduct an appropriate Post Incident Review or Debrief.

#### Purpose
This Operational Method Statement provides guidance on the establishment of incident sectors and outlines the roles and responsibilities of Sector Commanders.

#### Scope
This Operational Method Statement applies all FRV Operational Personnel.

#### Actions

**1. General requirements**
- **1.1** Establish incident sectors with appointed Sector Commanders at incidents where the scale and complexity is likely to limit the Incident Controller’s situational awareness, particularly where:
  - operations are taking place in more than one location, or remotely from the Incident Control Point.
  - the span of control on the fireground exceeds 1:5.
  - technical operations are taking place.
- **1.2** Ensure the creation and location of incident sectors is only established under instruction from the Incident Controller.
- **1.3** Allocate appropriately ranked and experienced personnel to the role of Sector Commander where available:
  - **1.3.1** Utilise a Leading Firefighter as a minimum.
  - **1.3.2** Utilise a Station Officer or Senior Station Officer for all 3rd alarm incidents and above.
  - **1.3.3** Ensure any support agency personnel allocated to this role are suitably endorsed.
- **1.4** Appoint a Safety Officer to all sectors where resources permit.
- **1.5** Ensure all crews and appliances report directly to the Sector Commander for tasking.
- **1.6** Consider conducting Atmospheric Monitoring at designated Sector Command Points.

**2. Sector Commander roles and responsibilities**
- **2.1** Obtain a SMEACSQ briefing from the Operations Officer or Incident Controller.
- **2.2** Implement the section of the Incident Action Plan relevant to the sector, with consideration to RECEO and the Emergency Management Priorities published in the Victorian State Emergency Management Plan.
- **2.3** Brief all personnel allocated to the sector.
- **2.4** Allocate tasks to resources within the sector and maintain control of the resources.
- **2.5** Implement and monitor safety and welfare measures of all personnel within the sector.
- **2.6** Conduct regular Safe Person Approach, Dynamic Risk Assessments (SPADRA) and perform continual Size Up for the duration of the shift.
- **2.7** Provide regular strategic level Situation Reports through the chain of command.
- **2.8** Wear a tabard to identify the role.
- **2.9** Ensure the allocated crews work within the established Communications Plan, and monitor the effectiveness of communications.
  - **2.9.1** Maintain sufficient radios to monitor the allocated command and fireground channels.
- **2.10** Work with the Safety Officer appointed to the sector.
- **2.11** Ensure Rapid Intervention Teams (RIT) are formed where required and located in a ready status at appropriate locations for the sector.
- **2.12** Coordinate activities with adjoining sectors.
- **2.13** Respond additional resources for the sector via the chain of command when necessary.
- **2.14** Report all accidents, injuries, hazards or near misses through the chain of command.
- **2.15** Resolve problems as they arise.
- **2.16** Participate in development of plans for the next operational period.
- **2.17** Maintain a log of all activities.

**3. Establishing sectors – Low rise structure fires (up to 4 levels)**
- **3.1** Adopt the following sectorisation model for incidents involving low rise structures:
  - **3.1.1** Designate the front of the structure or location of the Incident Control Point as Sector 1, and then allocate additional sectors progressing clockwise in sequential numbers.

**4. Establishing sectors – Mid and high rise structure fires (over 4 levels)**
- **4.1** Establish vertical sectors for incidents involving mid and high rise structures. Adopt the following model where vertical sectors are to be designated:
  - **4.1.1** Establish external sectors in addition to the above model, in line with the low rise model where necessary.
- **4.2** Ensure Sector Commanders allocated to individual fire floors are situated on the allocated floor of operations, close to the stairwell exit where possible.
  - **4.2.1** Consider donning BA where pressurisation of stairwells has been compromised.
- **4.3** Establish an Operations Point with an appointed Operations Officer below the Fire Sector for high rise structure fires, preferably two floors below where possible, to manage all appointed Sector Commanders.
- **4.4** Designate the Lobby Sector to include the ground floor to the Operations Point floor.
  - **4.4.1** Appoint a Lobby Sector Commander to be positioned at the main entrance to the building.
  - **4.4.2** Ensure the Lobby Sector Commander assists with the movement of firefighting personnel up and down the structure, and the evacuees.
- **4.5** Designate the floor below the lowest reported floor of fire, and up to two floors above the highest reported floor of fire, as the Fire Sector.
- **4.6** Designate the area above the Fire Sector as the Evacuation Sector.
  - **4.6.1** Appoint an Evacuation Sector Commander to be positioned at the EWIS.

**5. Establishing sectors – structures with sub levels**
- **5.1** Adopt the following model at incidents involving sub levels within structures (i.e. basements):
- **5.2** Establish sectors applying the same principles as for high rise fires..
- **5.3** Designate all floors below, and two floors above the Fire Sector, as the Evacuation Sector.
- **5.4** Appoint an Evacuation Sector Commander to be positioned at the Incident Control Point or Operations Point.
- **5.5** Establish a Lobby Sector exterior from the buildings main entrance.
- **5.6** Establish external sectors in addition to the above model, in line with the low rise model where necessary.

**6. Establishing sectors - Bushfire and non-structure fires**
- **6.1** Sectorise bushfires and non-structure fires involving large geographical areas according to fire behaviour, geographical location, topographical boundaries and other safety factors.
- **6.2** Identify sectors utilising a physical feature such as a road, town, aspect, geographical area, or consider utilising the operational function (e.g. Hazmat Sector, Rescue Sector).
  - **6.2.1** Ensure that clear delineated sector borders/boundaries are established and understood with fires/incidents spread across large geographical areas.
- **6.3** Establish Sector Command Points at a location that meets the following conditions:
  - **6.3.1** Easily identifiable using a geographical or physical feature, such as cross roads, parking areas, bridges or tracks.
  - **6.3.2** Enables the Sector Commander to capture oncoming sector resources and allocate tasks.
  - **6.3.3** Provides for clear communications.
  - **6.3.4** Provides a good overview of the sector.
  - **6.3.5** Allows for enough parking room for staging of oncoming appliances.
  - **6.3.6** Is safe from the fire/incident and allows quick and easy access to safe zones.
  - **6.3.7** Is safe from road traffic.
- **6.4** Consider allocating an appropriate vehicle to a Sector Command Point to assist with management of the sector.

#### Purpose
This Operational Method Statement outlines the requirements when conducting a Size Up at all incidents.

#### Scope
This Operational Method Statement applies to all Operational Personnel.

#### Actions

**1. En-route**
- **1.1** Commence Size Up while en-route to incident.
- **1.2** Consider the following:
  - Any existing pre-plans or Site Specific Risk Information (e.g. flammable cladding, height of structure, hoarding, criminal activity, fuel load, dangerous animals)
  - Alarmed premises with keys held on station
  - Any further information provided from the Communications Centre
  - Local knowledge
  - Current and forecast weather conditions
  - Time of day
  - Potential community exposure and impacts
  - Potential infrastructure exposure and impacts
  - Consider issuing early Community Information/Warning
  - Fire Services jurisdiction
  - Potential water points
  - Columns of smoke and/or gas clouds.

**2. On scene**
- **2.1** Conduct a thorough Size Up within the physical and environmental limitations of the scene.
  - **2.1.1** Provide a word back when Size Up is suitably completed. If more time is needed, send a word back of ‘investigation’.
  - **2.1.2** Incident Controllers should avoid entering dangerous environments during Size Up, including smoke, gas or vapour clouds and potential structural collapse zones.
  - **2.1.3** Attempt to conduct a 360o Size Up except where physical and safety limitations exist.
  - **2.1.4** Consider requesting other Operational Personnel to assist in completing Size Up if circumstances impede the ability to do this safely, or if the incident is large or complex in nature. Ensure appropriate PPC and PPE is utilised.
- **2.2** Ensure the following principles are included in Size Up:
  - Facts – What do you know that is affecting the incident, mitigation and safety?
  - Probabilities – What is likely to happen, including potential for fire spread and risk to life?
  - Own situation – Do you have sufficient resources and capabilities? Should you respond more?
  - Decision – What is your objective for the incident?
  - Plan – How do you plan to resolve the incident, and what strategies and tactics will be applied?
- **2.3** Manage any immediate safety hazards and associated risks that become evident during a Size Up by performing a Safe Person Approach, Dynamic Risk Assessment (SPADRA).
- **2.4** Create an Incident Emergency Management Team (IEMT) with on-scene emergency services and liaise with any on-site representatives, occupants, technicians or witnesses to gather information, such as:
  - Nature of premises/occupancy status
  - Risk to life and evacuation status
  - Fuel types and fuel loads
  - Potential exposures
  - Known hazards
  - Access/egress paths
  - On-site intelligence (property plans, Emergency Information book/manifest).
  - **2.4.1** Clarify the role of the on-site building representative/s.
- **2.5** Utilise B-SAHF during Size Up at a structure fire:
  - Building – construction style/materials that impact fire behaviour
  - Smoke – volume, velocity, density, and colour
  - Air track – inlets and outlets, what is the building ventilation profile?
  - Heat – blackening/crazing of windows, blistering of paintwork
  - Flame – colour (yellow/red/blue), indicator of oxygen supply to fire

**3. Ongoing Size Up throughout incident**
- **3.1** Continue to apply the Size Up process throughout the duration of the incident.
- **3.2** Consider utilising other information sources and additional capabilities throughout the incident to gather ongoing intelligence when appropriate, such as:
  - Thermal Imaging Cameras
  - Aerial appliances
  - Spot weather checks
  - Atmospheric monitoring, plume modelling and FRV Scientific Advisors
  - Structural integrity assessment
  - Air observers and Remote Piloted Aircraft Systems
  - Rapid Impact Assessment Teams and Ground Observer Teams.
- **3.3** Additional information gathered during ongoing Size Up should, where appropriate, influence changes in the Incident Action Plan.

#### Purpose
This Operational Method Statement provides information regarding strategic and tactical level Situation Reports, including the required reporting format.

#### Scope
This Operational Method Statement applies to all Operational Personnel.

#### Actions

**1. General Requirements**
- **1.1** Tailor Situation Reports to either a Strategic or Tactical Level, depending on the roles and tasks being performed.
- **1.2** Precede all Situation Reports with the pro-word “Sitrep”.

**2. Strategic Level Situation Report**
- **2.1** Strategic Level Situation Reports are to contain information relevant to the incident strategies and objective(s).
- **2.2** Incident Controllers are to provide Strategic Level Situation Reports to the Communication Centre at the earliest possible time for escalating incidents, and then periodically throughout the incident.
- **2.3** Operations Officers, Sector Commanders and Strike Team Leaders are to use Strategic Level Situation Reports to communicate information to the next level up the chain of command i.e. Sector Commander to Operations Officer or Operations Officer to Incident Controller etc.
- **2.4** Use the following format for all Strategic Level Situation Reports:
  - Incident type and status
  - Incident potential – risks to life and property
  - Loss and damage
  - Incident objective(s)
  - Likely resource requirements and commitment
  - Community warnings issued.
- **2.5** Consider sending a Strategic Level Situation Report in the following circumstances:
  - An emergency or priority situation such as Mayday or loss of PAR
  - Upon request from the Communications Centre
  - Changes to the IAP
  - Significant community evacuations or impacts OMS 012 – Situation Reports
  - In support of an incident escalation or Red Flag Warning.
  - Any other reason deemed necessary.

**3. Tactical Level Situation Report**
- **3.1** Tactical Level Situation Reports are to only contain information relevant to an assigned task and must be kept brief.
- **3.2** Single resources are to use Tactical Level Situation Reports to communicate key information up the chain of command to personnel performing functional roles i.e. Firefighter to Appliance OIC or Appliance OIC to Sector Commander etc.
- **3.3** Use the CAN format for all Tactical Level Situation Reports:
  - Conditions – What are the current conditions of the incident/task?
  - Actions – What actions are being implemented?
  - Needs – What additional resources are required?
- **3.4** Consider sending a Tactical Level Situation Report in the following circumstances:
  - Upon request from the chain of command
  - Periodically while undertaking a task
  - New critical information is discovered
  - Assigned tasks are completed or unable to be completed
  - When further resources are required or no longer required.

#### Purpose
This Operational Method Statement provides guidance on maintaining personnel accountability at incidents, including the requirements and process for conducting a Personnel Accountability Report (PAR).

#### Scope
This Operational Method Statement applies to all FRV Operational Personnel.

#### Actions

**1. Maintaining Personnel Accountability**
- **1.1** Ensure Fast Cards are completed and accurately reflect appliance crews. This is the responsibility of the OIC of the appliance.
- **1.2** Ensure all OICs of appliances report to the Incident Control Point for tasking upon arrival at an incident.
  - **1.2.1** Continue to report to, and receive tasking from, the chain of command to maintain accountability.
- **1.3** Avoid splitting appliance crews where practicable. Appliances should be directed to complete a task as a unit where possible.
  - **1.3.1** Consider the following options where an appliance OIC is utilised to perform a role where their crew is not required:
    - Assign a LFF to assume the role of crew leader, if available.
    - Reassign crew to another appliance OIC.
- **1.4** Ensure personnel performing functional roles account for resources under their command.
  - **1.4.1** Ensure systems are set up that allow for an appropriate span of control.
- **1.5** Maintain accountability when supervising a resource, team or functional role. Ensure all radio calls to allocated call sign are answered, and immediately report any loss of personnel accountability as soon as possible.

**2. Conducting a Personnel Accountability Report**
- **2.1** Conduct a PAR when any of the following situations occur:
  - Receipt of a Mayday message
  - Use of the emergency evacuation signal
  - A change from offensive to defensive strategies
  - Crews are failing to respond.

**OMS 013 – Personnel Accountability Reports**
- **2.2** Consider conducting a PAR in the following situations:
  - A change of Incident Controller or Sector Commander.
  - Any other reason at the discretion of an authorising officer.
- **2.3** Ensure a PAR is only requested by the following authorised personnel for their area of accountability:
  - Incident Controller
  - Operations Officer
  - Safety Officer
  - Sector Commander
  - BA Entry Officer (BAEO).

**3. Communicating a PAR**
- **3.1** Ensure only the IC or Communications Centre requests a PAR via the dispatch channel to determine resources en-route and on scene.
- **3.2** Ensure all authorised personnel request a PAR via an allocated fireground channel to determine accountability of resources.
- **3.3** Confirm accountability with the pro-word “PAR”.

**4. Unaccounted for resources**
- **4.1** Continue to try and make contact with any unaccounted for appliances, resources or personnel in the situation of a failed PAR.
- **4.2** Send a nearby resource(s) to the last known location of any unaccounted for personnel to try and make contact.
- **4.3** Issue a Mayday message if a resource remains unaccounted for.
- **4.4** Utilise RIT to begin searching for unaccounted resources where appropriate.

#### Purpose
This Operational Method Statement outlines the process for issuing and receiving Red Flag Warnings during operational incidents.

#### Scope
This Operational Method Statement applies to all Operational Personnel.

#### Actions

**1. Red Flag Warnings**
- **1.1** Consider issuing a Red Flag Warning when a change in circumstances presents a significant risk to safety, or is predicted to present a significant risk to safety. This may include but is not limited to the following:
  - Weather conditions
  - Fuel conditions
  - Incident/fire behaviour
  - Potential hazardous atmosphere
  - Equipment availability
  - Communications issues/difficulties
  - Access issues/difficulties
  - Structural collapse
  - LPG BLEVE or other possible explosion.

**2. Red Flag Warning responsibility**
- **2.1** Ensure Red Flag Warnings are only issued by the following personnel, in their area of responsibility, for the geographical area likely to be affected by the changed circumstances at a specific incident:
  - Sector Commander
  - Division Commander
  - Operations Officer
  - Incident Controller. Note: A Regional Controller, State and Regional Agency Commanders, State Duty Officer, Assistant Chief Fire Officer and the rostered Area or District Duty Officer may issue a Red Flag Warning via an Incident Controller.

**3. Requirements for issuing a Red Flag Warning**
- **3.1** Ensure Red Flag Warnings are preceded by the words “Red Flag Warning” and then issued as follows: “Red Flag Warning from (insert position and name). All personnel are advised of (actual/forecast where appropriate) conditions that may present a hazard to personnel as follows (actual/forecast conditions). All personnel are to take this information into account in determining a strategy, tactics and deployment. This warning is to be passed to all personnel under your command and is current up to hrs / / . Acknowledgement is required.
- **3.2** Convey Red Flag Warnings by any appropriate means, including:
  - Radio
  - Telephone
  - Written notice
  - Verbal
- **3.3** Ensure a Red Flag Warning broadcast via radio takes priority over all other radio traffic, except for a Mayday and Red, Red, Red priority message.
- **3.4** Ensure the message is specific to the key audience (e.g. Sector 3) to minimise radio congestion.
- **3.5** Ensure any Red Flag Warnings issued by a person performing a fireground functional role under AIIMS, communicates the Red Flag Warning up the chain of command to the Incident Controller.
- **3.6** Inform Communications Centre when a Red Flag Warning has been issued, including the details of the warning. The Incident Controller is responsible for informing Communications Centre.
- **3.7** Ensure all members of an established IEMT are informed of the Red Flag Warning details. The Incident Controller is responsible for informing the IEMT.
- **3.8** Document/log all details of the Red Flag Warning, including:
  - Name of person who issued the Red Flag Warning
  - The time it was issued
  - The information it contained
  - How it was issued
  - Who it was issued to and who was informed (both up and down the chain of command)
  - The time acknowledgements were received from those you supervise.

**4. Requirements for receiving a Red Flag Warning**
- **4.1** Ensure personnel who receive a Red Flag Warning complete the following:
  - Confirm the Red Flag Warning has been received immediately.
  - Repeat the key points of the warning back to the sender to demonstrate understanding.
  - Notify all responding and support agency personnel of the Red Flag Warning under your supervision/in reporting line.
  - Obtain a confirmation from these personnel that they have received the warning.
- **4.2** Ensure any personnel performing a fireground functional role under AIIMS who has received a Red Flag Warning documents/logs all details of the message, including:
  - Name of person who issued the Red Flag Warning
  - The time it was issued
  - The information it contained
  - How it was issued
  - Who you issued it to and informed (both up and down the chain of command)
  - The time acknowledgements were received from those you supervise.
- **4.3** Use all possible measures to ensure the intended recipient receives the message where a person or unit does not acknowledge a Red Flag Warning.

**5. Cancelling a Red Flag Warning**
- **5.1** Ensure personnel are notified once the dangerous situation has concluded, if no timing was given in the warning when issued. This should be done by normal means of communication.

**6. Examples of Red Flag Warning dissemination and acknowledgement**
- **6.1** Bushfire
- **6.2** Urban incident

#### Purpose
This Operational Method Statement provides information regarding Mayday radio messages, including actions required for issuing a Mayday message and reacting to these messages on the fireground.

#### Scope
This Operational Method Statement applies to all Operational Personnel.

#### Actions

**1. Issuing a Mayday Radio Message**
- **1.1** Transmit a Mayday immediately when in a life-threatening situation, or when others are in a life-threatening situation.
- **1.2** Utilise the Radio Duress Alarm (where available) to initiate the Mayday, and immediately transmit the following:
  - “Mayday, Mayday, Mayday”
  - Name of person transmitting or unit/call sign
  - Location
  - Situation report/assignment/task
  - Resources/assistance

**2. Receiving a Mayday Radio Message**
- **2.1** Prioritise Mayday messages over Red, Red, Red priority signals, and all other radio messages.
- **2.2** Cease all other radio traffic upon hearing a Mayday message.
- **2.3** Respond to the Mayday message immediately and assume control of the response. This is to be completed by the IC or a delegated person, and is to include the following:
  - Confirm the details provided by the caller.
  - Commit resources to the intervention effort including any pre-formed RIT.
  - Establish a Rescue Sector (as determined by the IC).
  - Allocate appropriate radio channels to the intervention effort.
  - Issue a general message or a Red Flag Warning to the fire/incident channels, if appropriate.
- **2.4** Ensure only resources within the immediate vicinity render assistance at the direction of the IC or delegate.
- **2.5** Ensure all other crews continue to combat the fire or incident.
- **2.6** Acknowledge receipt of Mayday message and relay the message to Communications Centre if Communications Centre have not acknowledged the Mayday caller and stopped all other transmissions.

**3. Concluding a Mayday Situation**
- **3.1** Ensure the following is completed once the Mayday situation has been resolved:
  - Notify Communications Centre
  - Notify all personnel on the fireground
  - Ensure any Duress Alarms activated have been reset
  - Resume prioritising the combating of the fire or incident.

**4. Use of ‘Mayday’ During Training**
- **4.1** Notify FSCC (via telephone 03 9665 4397) of the planned training drill and the intent to utilise Duress button and transmit a Mayday call.
- **4.2** Utilise a LOCAL channel (Zone Selector C) designated to the District or the FSCC can allocate FG Channel 55 which is unmonitored at Triple Zero Victoria
  - If utilising a local channel advise the FSCC which channel will be used.
  - Regional stations can utilise the RMR FSCC Training Channel which can be allocated by the FSCC - 1300 833 278
- **4.3** Provide training location and contact details of Officer In Charge.
- **4.4** Prior to drill commencing, ensure all participants have selected and are locked on the assigned local training channel.
- **4.5** Immediately prior to the Mayday call or Duress activation, transmit “For training purposes only”.
- **4.6** Immediately after the duress/mayday drill - complete your transmission with "Training Completed"
- **4.7** Notify the FSCC when training drill has been completed and training channels are no longer required.
- **4.8** Ensure all radios are changed back to original channel once training is completed.
- **4.9** If an actual Mayday message is required during training, issue as per Actions 1 to 3.

#### Purpose
This Operational Method Statement provides information regarding Red, Red, Red Priority Signals, including actions required for issuing and reacting to these messages on the fireground.

#### Scope
This Operational Method Statement applies to all Operational Personnel.

#### Actions

**1. Issuing a Red, Red, Red Priority Signal**
- **1.1** Transmit a “Red, Red, Red” signal to send an urgent message where extreme radio congestion exists, in order to gain priority access to Communications Centre and the fireground channel(s). Scenarios where this may be required include the following:
  - A word back message requiring the escalation of an incident.
  - A general message communicating a significant fireground safety issue.
  - A Red Flag Warning.
- **1.2** Press the radio Press to Talk (PTT) button, and state “Red, Red, Red” prior to issuing the urgent message.
- **1.3** Utilise the Duress Alarm function if still unable to communicate, in order to gain priority access to transmit a Red, Red, Red Priority Signal.
- **1.4** Send a Mayday radio message in life threatening situations.
- **1.5** Respond to any requests from Communications Centre for a Sitrep.
- **1.6** Ensure the Duress Alarm is reset at the earliest practicable time when it has been used to transmit the Red, Red, Red Priority Signal.

**2. Hearing a Red, Red, Red Priority Signal – Dispatch Channels (Communications Centre)**
- **2.1** Cease all other radio transmissions upon hearing a Red, Red, Red Priority Signal, as these take precedence over all other radio transmissions, except for Mayday messages. Communications Centre will stop all other transmissions and acknowledge the priority caller.

**3. Hearing a Red, Red, Red Priority Signal – Fireground Channels**
- **3.1** Cease all other radio transmissions upon hearing a Red, Red, Red Priority Signal on a fireground channel, and allow the urgent message to be completed before recommencing radio transmissions.
- **3.2** Ensure that the urgent message is responded to as required.
notes.ref: OMS 016 – Red, Red, Red Priority Signal
